newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industrial output up strongly in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industrial output up strongly in December.

text.p: U.S. industrial output increased strongly in December as brisk manufacturing business pushed industry to its fastest operating rates in more than a year, the Federal Reserve said Friday.

Total industrial output climbed a stronger-than-expected 0.8 percent after a revised identical 0.8 percent increase in November. The gain would have been even stronger except for mild weather that cut electrical utilities' prodution, the Fed said.

The central bank said that U.S. industry was running at 83.8 percent of its maximum capacity during December, up from a revised 83.4 percent in November and the fastest rate since 83.9 percent in August 1995.

The sharp pickup in capacity use rates may raise a red flag about potential inflationary pressures becasue it indicates strong demand for goods needed in manufacturing processes. Prices for bonds dipped shortly after the industrial output report was released but later recovered.

Output by manufacturing industries jumped 1.1 percent in December after a 0.7 percent rise in November. The Fed said production of consumer goods, business equipment and non-energy materials advanced sharply in December.

Mining output was up 1.2 percent after a 0.6 percent increase in November. The only major sector that recorded weaker output in December was utilities, down 3.3 percent following a 2.3 percent rise in November.
The Fed blamed that on a mild start to the winter that reduced heating demands.
"The unseasonably mild weather in December caused a large drop in the output of utilities, reducing the growth rate of overall production by about 0.3 percentage point," the Fed said.

For the fourth quarter as a whole, U.S. industrial output increased 4.1 percent, down from a 4.5 percent gain in the third quarter. But the Fed said fourth-quarter output was held back by disruptions to production in the auto industry. A strike in Canada during October temporarily curbed new-car production rates at industry leader General Motors Corp.
The strike has since been settled and production has returned to normal.
